title: Design caching, configuration and automated deployment
learningObjective: Recommend a caching solution, an application configuration management solution, and an automated deployment solution for applications.
foundation: Caching keeps frequently used data close and fast, so the database does less work.
Configuration management keeps settings and feature flags in one place, outside the code.
Automated deployment builds and releases the app the same way every time, with infrastructure described as code.
engineer: Caching: Azure Managed Redis (the successor to Azure Cache for Redis, which is being retired) for distributed cache, session state, rate limiting and pub/sub, with patterns such as cache-aside and TTL-based expiry; edge caching with Azure Front Door for static and cacheable content; API Management response caching; Cosmos DB integrated cache; in-memory caches in the app for per-instance data.

Configuration: Azure App Configuration for central key-values, labels per environment, feature flags (with filters such as percentage rollout) and dynamic refresh; Key Vault for secrets (App Configuration stores Key Vault references); managed identities to read both; App Service and Functions settings with Key Vault references for simple apps.

Automated deployment: infrastructure as code (Bicep or Terraform; template specs and deployment stacks for governed reuse); CI/CD with GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines using workload identity federation; deployment strategies: deployment slots with swap (App Service), revisions with traffic splitting (Container Apps), blue-green and canary on AKS; environments with approvals; Azure Deployment Environments for developer self-service.

example.title: Shipping faster and safer
body: Product lookups use cache-aside with Azure Managed Redis; images are cached at the edge by Front Door. Settings live in App Configuration with labels per environment; secrets stay in Key Vault.

GitHub Actions deploys Bicep and code on every merge using workload identity federation; new versions go to a staging slot, are warmed up and swapped; a feature flag enables the new checkout for 10% of users.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription; most design reviews need only Reader access
permissions: Reader to review existing resources; Contributor or Owner to build the design
limits: Check service limits and regional availability for each component
portal: App Configuration > Configuration explorer, Feature manager.
Azure Managed Redis: create cache, choose tier and size.
App Service > Deployment slots; Deployment Center (GitHub Actions).

troubleshooting.symptom: Users see stale prices after updates.
troubleshooting.cause: Cache entries never expire or aren't invalidated.
troubleshooting.fix: Set a TTL and invalidate on write (cache-aside).

troubleshooting.symptom: Changing a setting requires redeploying 20 services.
troubleshooting.fix: Move them to App Configuration with dynamic refresh.

comparisons.difference: App Configuration for settings and feature flags; Key Vault for secrets, keys and certificates.
Both allow staged rollout; slots swap whole apps, revisions split traffic by percentage.

misconceptions.reality: It holds copies that can disappear; the source of truth stays in the database.
Infrastructure should be deployed by the same pipelines as code.

architectureDecisions: Cache-aside with Azure Managed Redis; edge caching for static content.
App Configuration + Key Vault references, read with managed identity.
IaC + CI/CD with federated credentials; slots or revisions for safe rollout.

walkthrough.subtitle: Make the app fast with caching, easy to change with central configuration, and safe to release with automation.
learn: Configuration: App Configuration and Key Vault

steps.label: Problem
steps.title: Slow pages, scattered settings, risky releases
body: The database is overloaded with the same reads, every service has its own settings file, and releases happen by hand on Friday nights.

steps.label: Cache
steps.title: Keep hot data close
body: Cache-aside: check Redis first; on a miss, read the database and store the result with an expiry. Front Door caches static files near users.

steps.label: Config
steps.title: One place for settings
body: App Configuration holds settings and feature flags for every service, per environment. Secrets stay in Key Vault and are referenced. Apps read both with their managed identity.

steps.label: Deploy
steps.title: Automate and release safely
body: Bicep or Terraform describe the infrastructure; GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines build and deploy on every merge; a staging slot is warmed up and swapped into production.

steps.title: App platform design
